title: Closures and generics
summary: Functions as values that remember their surroundings, and type parameters for reusable code.
hints: `Counter` returns a closure over a variable declared *outside* the returned function: `n := 0; return func() int { n++; return n }`. Each call to `Counter()` makes a fresh `n`, so two counters never interfere.

`MakeAdders(n)`: `for i := range n { adders = append(adders, func(x int) int { return x + i }) }`. Since Go 1.22 every iteration gets its *own* `i`, so each closure remembers a different value (in older Go they all shared one and printed the last). The generic helpers are plain loops: `Map` allocates `make([]U, len(xs))` and fills it, `Filter` appends the elements `keep` approves, and `Reduce` folds with `acc = f(acc, x)`.

`MaxOf[T cmp.Ordered](xs ...T) (T, bool)`: `cmp.Ordered` is the constraint for types that support `<`, so it works for ints, floats and strings alike. Return the zero value and `false` for no arguments (`var zero T; return zero, false`).
